mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate is held constant for two consecutive months above 1.5%, market expectations of future rate cuts diminish, lowering discount rates and boosting the present value of equity cash flows, thereby driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: FOMC holds rates steady in a restrictive environment
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not statistically higher than the 30-day average preceding the trigger, or discount rate spread (SPX spot vs. 10Y Treasury) widens during the window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly increase in CPIAUCSL by more than 0.3% followed by a sustained decline in FEDFUNDS within the same quarter is interpreted by markets as a shift toward price stability and rate easing, which elevates equity valuations and produces positive 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increases >0.3% in month X and FEDFUNDS decreases in month X+1
regime_hint: Inflation surprise followed by immediate rate cut anticipation
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative despite meeting the trigger, or the discount rate spread does not compress as expected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly rise in PAYEMS of at least 2% above the prior quarter's average indicates strengthening labor market conditions, which boosts consumer confidence and corporate earnings expectations, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases >2% month-on-quarter for two consecutive months
regime_hint: Labor market strengthening in the absence of wage inflation
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are negative, or unemployment rate (UNRATE) does not show a corresponding decline.

mechanism_narrative: When GDPC1 (real GDP) grows at an annualized rate above 3% for three consecutive quarters, it signals robust economic momentum that elevates risk premia and drives higher equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 annual growth >3% for three consecutive quarters
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative, or GDP revisions indicate slower growth in subsequent quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in INDPRO by more than 5% from the prior month, accompanied by a simultaneous rise in HOUST by at least 10%, signals weak industrial production and strong service demand, creating a supply imbalance that compresses real rates and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases >5% month-over-month AND HOUST increases >10% month-over-month
regime_hint: Industrial weakness coupled with service sector strength
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive after controlling for sector weights, or the supply-demand ratio (INDPRO/HOUST) does not deteriorate.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-time drop in UNRATE below 4% followed by two consecutive months of UNRATE stability at or above 3.8% creates a labor market softening that reduces wage growth expectations and supports equity risk appetite, producing a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 4% in a single month and remains ≥3.8% in the next two months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative, or wage growth (PAYEMS) shows a corresponding decline.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS rises by more than 0.25% in a single month during a period of elevated inflation (CPIAUCSL > 271), it signals a preemptive hike aimed at curbing demand, which typically precedes a short-term equity pullback and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 271 AND FEDFUNDS increases >0.25% in the same month
regime_hint: High-inflation environment with aggressive policy tightening
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative, or the S&P 500 does not experience the expected volatility spike.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in RSAFS of at least 15% for three consecutive months, in the absence of a corresponding rise in GDPC1, indicates weakening demand for financial assets and a risk-off environment that compresses equity valuations and drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS decreases >15% month-over-month for three consecutive months AND GDPC1 does not increase at a similar rate
regime_hint: Financial market stress with stable or declining real activity
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative after adjusting for sector-specific risk premia.
